audit.whatIsWrong: mid says 'when he commits, Solar Snare roots him, the field slows him 30%, and you back out'. Nothing anywhere notes that Decisive Strike breaks free of all slows.
audit.why: Riot's text for Decisive Strike is 'Garen gains a burst of Move Speed, breaking free of all slows affecting him.' Solar Snare roots at its centre and slows the area around it — so his Q deletes the outer slow field but has no answer to the centre root, which is not a slow. That converts a vague 'root and kite' into a precise aiming instruction: the orb has to land ON him, not near him. It is also the single most abusable detail in the matchup.
audit.corrected: Decisive Strike breaks the outer slow field; the centre root is not a slow and still holds. Land the orb on him.
sources: champ-data/_kits/garen.json (Q: 'breaking free of all slows affecting him')
champ-data/_kits/mel.json (E: 'rooting those at its center while the area around it slows')

audit.whatIsWrong: Four places write the same non-interaction instead of the real one: spikes[2].text 'you chain-poke and W back his... nothing — he has no projectile'; whys[2] 'he has no projectile to fear the wall, so it's a free shield'; wants.foe[1] 'Bait W's projectile wall (he has none)'; early 'there's nothing for it to eat since Garen has no projectile'.
audit.why: Beyond being filler, the conclusion drawn from it is wrong. Rebuttal is not a 'free shield' here — Decisive Strike silences, and a silenced Mel cannot cast Rebuttal or Solar Snare at all. The W is a timing problem: it has to be up before the dash connects, never after. The current text tells the player the opposite, that she can relax about the ability.
audit.corrected: Decisive Strike silences — Rebuttal has to go up before the dash lands, because after it the cast is denied.
sources: champ-data/_kits/mel.json (W, E both require a cast)

audit.whatIsWrong: mid states the slow field 'slows him 30%'.
audit.why: No slow percentage for Solar Snare exists anywhere on disk — the kit carries cooldowns, costs and ranges but no magnitudes. The figure is unsupported, and it is attached to the one effect Decisive Strike removes outright.
audit.corrected: Dropped the invented number and replaced it with the root-versus-slow distinction that is verifiable.
sources: champ-data/_kits/mel.json (E description carries no slow magnitude)

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags zero cooldown-sequencing cues, and the full layer tracks 'Courage' as the matchup-defining ability, warning against 'standing inside Courage range'.
audit.why: Courage is self-cast with range 0 — there is no Courage range to stand in. Garen's threat ability is Decisive Strike, a flat 8s that carries the silence, the slow-break and his only gap-close. Courage matters for a different reason the text never gives: it grants tenacity, so a pre-cast W shortens Mel's root.
audit.corrected: Decisive Strike 8s flat, Courage 22s at rank 1 (shield, damage cut, tenacity), Judgment 9s, Demacian Justice 120s, Mel's Rebuttal 38s.

audit.whatIsWrong: early says his passive 'heals chip if you let him reset' without saying what breaks it.
audit.why: Perseverance only regenerates if Garen has not recently been struck by damage OR enemy abilities. For a 950-range volley on a 10s cooldown that is a switch Mel can hold off permanently — a single tick of Radiant Volley turns his sustain off, which is why he cannot win a poke war he never gets to reset out of.
audit.corrected: Any damage stops Perseverance; one volley tick keeps his regen switched off.

edits.before: At Level 1 just poke with Q and hold range — he can only walk at you and his passive regen heals chip if you let him reset, so deny his last-hits instead of trading for trades' sake. The lane flips at Level 2: with Q + Solar Snare you root him the moment he steps up for CS, then Q the rooted target and walk off before his Q silence range can touch you. By 3 you add W — there's nothing for it to eat since Garen has no projectile, so save it as a shield and the move-speed to peel his Q-dash and keep your spacing.
edits.after: At Level 1 just poke with Q and hold range — he can only walk at you, and Perseverance stops regenerating the moment any damage touches him, so chip him off it rather than trading for trades' sake. The lane flips at Level 2: with Q + Solar Snare you root him the moment he steps up for CS, then Q the rooted target and walk off before his Q silence range can touch you. By 3 you add W — Decisive Strike silences, so Rebuttal has to go up before the dash connects, and after that it is your shield and move speed to peel.

edits.before: This is your lane. His only gap-close is Decisive Strike (Q) and a Flash, so every all-in is telegraphed — when he commits, Solar Snare roots him, the field slows him 30%, and you back out while Overwhelm ticks. At 6 Golden Eclipse turns the stacks you've built into a ranged execute that beats his passive regen, so poke him to ~40% and detonate. Respect his Q silence only when he's actually on top of you — it cancels your cast, so don't be mid-animation when he lands the dash.
edits.after: This is your lane. His only gap-close is Decisive Strike (Q) and a Flash, so every all-in is telegraphed — but Decisive Strike breaks free of all slows, so Solar Snare's outer field will not hold him. The centre root is not a slow, so land the orb ON him and he stays put. At 6 Golden Eclipse turns the stacks you've built into a ranged execute that beats Perseverance, so poke him to ~40% and detonate. His Q silence cancels your cast, so never be mid-animation when the dash lands.

edits.before: You win this lane outright, but late Garen stops being a lane and becomes a statcheck — Stridebreaker and tank items let him eat your poke and his missing-HP true-damage R executes your squishy frame the instant he reaches you. His W also cuts your burst and gives tenacity, shortening your root. Close the game on your first-item dominance; if it goes long, never get caught without Flash, because one Q-Flash-silence chain is all he needs to delete you.
edits.after: You win this lane outright, but late Garen stops being a lane and becomes a statcheck — Stridebreaker and tank items let him eat your poke and his missing-HP true-damage R executes your squishy frame the instant he reaches you. Courage is 22s at rank 1 and gives tenacity on top of the shield, so a pre-cast shortens your root every time. Close the game on your first-item dominance; if it goes long, never get caught without Flash.

notes: The most useful thing in this matchup was absent from both layers: Decisive Strike breaks free of all slows, so Solar Snare's outer slow field is worthless against Garen while its centre root — not a slow — still holds him. That turns 'root and kite' into 'land the orb on him'. Second: four places said some version of 'Garen has no projectile so W is free', which is both a non-interaction and the wrong conclusion, because Decisive Strike's silence denies the Rebuttal cast outright — the W is a pre-emptive tool here, not a reactive one. Also removed an invented '30%' slow figure (no slow magnitudes exist anywhere on disk) and repointed the full layer's cooldown tracking off Courage, which is self-cast with range 0 so 'standing inside Courage range' was meaningless. Full-layer verdict fields remain uncorrectable through the applier (shared boilerplate, exactly-once rule).
